findings.title: Required checks run PR-editable code outside the CODEOWNERS owner surface; a one-line edit turns pr-contract green
findings.claim: 8 tracked files that required-context jobs run from the pull request's own checkout have no CODEOWNERS owner. 3 of them are modules that pr-contract's policy_lint.mjs loads, and appending one line to any of those 3 turns pr-contract's refusal of an empty body (rc=1) into a pass (rc=0). So the check can be changed with only the hpo-approver App's review, even though .github/CODEOWNERS says the whole enforcement surface is owner-owned.
findings.mechanism: CODEOWNERS derives its surface from R6's codeowners_gap.py rule. That rule counts a script only when a line calls it through an interpreter (node/python3/bash ...), and it never follows imports. It therefore misses the bare `./tests/run.sh` (fast), the bare `./tests/derive_closures.sh` (closures), and every module an owned entry script imports: counts.mjs and render_md.mjs (imported by policy_lint.mjs; counts.mjs also by brief_lint.mjs) and vendor/markdown-it.min.js (required by render_md.mjs). Unlike policy-docs, pr-contract and briefs do not restore their check source from the base commit before they grade, so the PR's own copies run.

findings.title: release.yml publishes and attests any v* tag or dispatch ref with no check that the commit is on main
findings.claim: release.yml's release job was run step by step in a scratch clone. It reaches `gh release create` and the signed tree digest for an unmerged branch commit in 2 of 2 event paths (tag push, workflow_dispatch), the same as for a commit on main. Its only refusal is the vN.N.N tag-name shape.
findings.mechanism: The workflow triggers on any pushed v* tag, and on dispatch it creates the tag at GITHUB_SHA. No step checks that the commit is an ancestor of origin/main. hpo-author's installation token carries contents: write (decision 0011), which is enough to push a tag. Whether a GitHub tag ruleset blocks that push cannot be read through the available MCP tools; the recorded fixture names only branch rulesets. HACS installs from the latest v* release, so a commit that no required check or review gated could ship to users with a provenance attestation.

findings.title: Scorecard Pinned-Dependencies: 12 CI install commands are version-pinned but not hash-pinned
findings.claim: 12 dependency-install commands in tests.yml would count as unpinned under Scorecard's Pinned-Dependencies definition (a dependency 'explicitly set to a specific hash'): 9 `pip install -r tests/requirements-ci.txt` with no --hash lines, the typing venv install (5 names with no version at all), `pip install coverage==7.13.1`, and `npm install`/`npx` for playwright. Every `uses:` ref is SHA-pinned (0 unpinned).
findings.mechanism: The repository pinned action refs by commit (#960), but package installs are pinned by version, or not at all for the 5 typing third-party names, which are unversioned by design in tests/typing_ruler.py:requirement_lines.
